subject: Physics
title: NTA CUET (UG) Physics — 29 May 2024
instructions: Attempt only 40 questions out of the given 50 questions.
One mark will be deducted for a wrong answer.

questions.prompt: The kinetic energy of an electron in the ground level of a hydrogen atom is K units. The values of its potential energy and total energy respectively are _______.

steps.label: Recall Bohr-orbit energy relations
steps.detail: For an electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom, Kinetic Energy (KE) = K.

steps.label: Potential energy
steps.detail: $PE = -2 \times KE = -2K$.

steps.label: Total energy
steps.detail: $TE = KE + PE = K - 2K = -K$.

questions.why: In the Bohr model the potential energy is always minus twice the kinetic energy, so with KE = K the potential energy is −2K and the total energy is K − 2K = −K.

questions.prompt: Two nuclei have mass numbers A and B respectively. The density ratio of the nuclei is _______.

steps.label: Key fact
steps.detail: The density of a nucleus is independent of its mass number.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.detail: Therefore, the density ratio of any two nuclei is always $1 : 1$.

questions.why: Nuclear density is a constant (~2.3 × 10^17 kg/m³) independent of mass number, so any two nuclei have a density ratio of 1 : 1.

questions.prompt: A point source causing photoelectric emission from a metallic plate is moved away from the plate. The variation of photoelectric current with distance from the source is correctly represented by the graph _______.
options: Graph (a): photoelectric current increases linearly with distance
Graph (b): photoelectric current rises with distance and saturates
Graph (c): photoelectric current falls off sharply with distance (like $1/d^2$), levelling off
Graph (d): photoelectric current decreases linearly with distance
questions.answer: (c) Graph (c): photoelectric current falls off sharply with distance (like $1/d^2$), levelling off

steps.label: Intensity falls with distance
steps.detail: As the point source is moved away from the metallic plate, the intensity of light falling on the plate decreases with distance.

steps.label: Current follows intensity
steps.detail: This decrease in intensity reduces the photoelectric current; the correct graph showing this inverse relationship is graph (c).

questions.why: Intensity from a point source falls as 1/d², and photoelectric current is proportional to intensity, so the current decays like 1/d² with distance — the steeply falling curve (c).
questions.figure: Four graphs of photoelectric current vs distance: (a) straight line rising from origin; (b) rising curve that saturates; (c) curve falling steeply like 1/d² and levelling off toward zero; (d) straight line falling with distance.

questions.prompt: A proton accelerated through a potential difference V has a de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. On doubling the accelerating potential, de Broglie wavelength of the proton _______.

steps.label: de Broglie relation
steps.detail: $\lambda = h/\sqrt{2meV}$, where h is Planck's constant, m the mass, e the charge, and V the potential difference.

steps.label: Double the potential
steps.detail: $\lambda' = h/\sqrt{2me(2V)} = \lambda/\sqrt{2}$.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.detail: Thus the de Broglie wavelength decreases.

questions.why: Since λ ∝ 1/√V, doubling the accelerating potential reduces the wavelength by a factor of √2 — it decreases.

questions.prompt: The shortest wavelengths emitted in hydrogen spectrum corresponding to different spectral series are as under: A. Pfund series, B. Balmer series, C. Brackett series, D. Lyman series. The wavelengths arranged correctly in decreasing order are ______.

steps.label: Series limits
steps.detail: Lyman series (n = 1, n = ∞) has the shortest wavelength; Balmer (n = 2), Brackett (n = 4), Pfund (n = 5, longest wavelength).

steps.label: Order
steps.detail: Decreasing wavelength order: Pfund (A), Brackett (C), Balmer (B), Lyman (D).

questions.why: The series-limit wavelength grows with the lower level n, so Pfund (n=5) > Brackett (n=4) > Balmer (n=2) > Lyman (n=1) — order (A), (C), (B), (D).

questions.prompt: Silicon can be doped using one of the following elements as dopant: A. Arsenic, B. Indium, C. Phosphorus, D. Boron. To get n-type semiconductor, the dopants that can be used are ______.

steps.label: n-type needs pentavalent dopants
steps.detail: For n-type semiconductors, elements with five valence electrons (pentavalent impurities) are used as dopants.

steps.label: Identify pentavalent elements
steps.detail: Arsenic (A) and Phosphorus (C) are pentavalent impurities, making them suitable for creating n-type semiconductors.

questions.why: n-type doping requires pentavalent atoms that donate an extra electron; of the list, only arsenic and phosphorus are pentavalent (indium and boron are trivalent, giving p-type).

questions.prompt: Given below are V versus I graphs for different types of p–n junction diodes marked A, B, C, and D. The correct sequence of graphs corresponding to forward biased p–n junction, Zener diode, photo diode, and solar cell in order is ______.

steps.label: Identify each graph
steps.detail: (A) is a photo diode — current proportional to light intensity with a reverse characteristic. (B) is a solar cell — shows short-circuit current ($I_{sc}$) and open-circuit voltage ($V_{oc}$).

steps.label: Remaining graphs
steps.detail: (C) is a Zener diode — sharp breakdown in reverse bias. (D) is a forward biased p–n junction diode — exponential increase in current with voltage.

steps.label: Sequence
steps.detail: Forward biased p–n junction, Zener, photo diode, solar cell → (D), (C), (A), (B).

questions.why: Matching each characteristic curve to its device (exponential forward rise = ordinary diode, reverse breakdown = Zener, reverse light-dependent current = photodiode, fourth-quadrant curve with Voc and Isc = solar cell) gives the sequence (D), (C), (A), (B).
questions.figure: Four I–V graphs with I(mA)/I(μA) axes vs v(volts). A: small reverse current growing in the third quadrant (photodiode-style reverse characteristic). B: fourth-quadrant curve crossing at V_oc (open-circuit voltage) on the +v axis and I_sc (short-circuit current) on the −I axis (solar cell). C: forward rise plus sharp near-vertical reverse breakdown at V_z (Zener), 'Forward bias' labelled. D: exponential current rise in forward bias only (ordinary p–n junction).

questions.prompt: A wire carrying current I, bent as shown in the figure, is placed in a uniform field B that emerges normally out of the plane of the figure. The force on this wire is ______.

steps.label: Force law
steps.detail: The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is $F = I(L \times B)$, where L is the length of the wire in the direction of the field.

steps.label: Straight segments
steps.detail: For the straight segments the force will be $2 \times BIR$ downward.

steps.label: Semicircular segment
steps.detail: For the semicircular segment of radius R the force is directed downward with $F = I(2R)B$, since the effective length of the semicircle is 2R.

steps.label: Total
steps.detail: Thus the force on the wire is 4BIR, vertically downward.

questions.why: Each part contributes a force B·I·(effective straight length): 2R from the two straight pieces and 2R (the diameter) from the semicircle, giving 4BIR directed vertically downward.
questions.figure: Wire from P (left) to Q (right) carrying current I: straight segment of length R, semicircular arc of radius R bulging upward, straight segment of length R. Dots fill the region indicating field B out of the plane.

questions.prompt: The refractive index of the material of an equilateral prism is $\sqrt{2}$. The angle of minimum deviation of that prism is ______.

steps.label: Minimum deviation formula
steps.detail: $n = \sin[(A + \delta_{min})/2]/\sin(A/2)$ with $A = 60°$ for an equilateral prism.

steps.label: Solve
steps.detail: $(60° + \delta_{min})/2 = 45°$, hence $60° + \delta_{min} = 90°$ and $\delta_{min} = 30°$.

questions.why: Applying the prism formula n = sin((A+δmin)/2)/sin(A/2) with n = √2 and A = 60° forces (60°+δmin)/2 = 45°, so the minimum deviation is 30°.

questions.prompt: The transfer of integral number of ______ is one of the evidence of quantization of electric charge.

steps.label: Quantization of charge
steps.detail: Quantization of electric charge means charge exists in discrete packets rather than in a continuous manner.

steps.label: Evidence
steps.detail: This is evidenced by the transfer of integral numbers of electrons, as electrons are the fundamental charge carriers.

questions.why: Charge changes only by whole multiples of e because charging happens by transfer of an integral number of electrons, the fundamental charge carriers.

questions.prompt: When a slab of insulating material 4 mm thick is introduced between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor of separation 4 mm, it is found that the distance between the plates has to be increased by 3.2 mm to restore the capacity to its original value. The dielectric constant of the material is ______.

steps.label: Capacitance with dielectric
steps.detail: $C = \kappa\varepsilon_0 A/d$; with a slab of thickness t the effective separation is $d_{eff} = d - t + t/\kappa$.

steps.label: Apply restore condition
steps.detail: The distance is increased by 3.2 mm to restore the capacity: $3.2 + 4/\kappa = 4$ (with $d - t = 3.2$ and $t = 4$).

steps.label: Solve
steps.detail: $\kappa = 5$.

questions.why: Inserting a slab of thickness t reduces the effective separation to d − t + t/κ; restoring the original capacitance after moving the plates 3.2 mm apart requires 3.2 + 4/κ = 4, so κ = 5.

questions.prompt: A copper ball of density 8.0 g/cc and 1 cm in diameter is immersed in oil of density 0.8 g/cc. The charge on the ball if it remains just suspended in oil in an electric field of intensity 600 N/C acting in the upward direction is ______. (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: (b) $2 \times 10^{-5}$ C (per the Answer Key; the paper's own explanation computes $6.288 \times 10^{-5}$ C and states 'no option match')

steps.label: Forces
steps.detail: Buoyant force $F_b = \rho_o V g = 4.192 \times 10^{-4}$ N (printed as $4.192 \times 10^{-3}$ N); electric force $F_e = qE$ with E = 600 N/C.

steps.label: Balance
steps.detail: $qE + \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\rho_o g = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\rho_{cu} g$, so $q = \frac{(4/3) \times 3.14 \times (0.005)^3 \times 7.2 \times 10^3 \times 10}{600}$.

steps.label: Result (as printed)
steps.detail: $q = 6.288 \times 10^{-5}$ C — 'no option match.' The Answer Key nevertheless marks (b).

questions.why: Balancing weight against buoyancy plus the upward electric force gives q = V(ρcu − ρoil)g / E; the paper's own arithmetic yields 6.288 × 10⁻⁵ C, which matches no option, though the key marks (b) 2 × 10⁻⁵ C.

questions.prompt: A metal wire is subjected to a constant potential difference. When the temperature of the metal wire increases, the drift velocity of the electron in it ______.
options: increases, thermal velocity of the electrons decreases
decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons decreases
increases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases
decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases
questions.answer: (d) decreases, thermal velocity of the electrons increases

steps.label: Effect of temperature on collisions
steps.detail: When the temperature increases, the lattice ions vibrate more vigorously, increasing the rate of collisions between electrons and ions.

steps.label: Consequences
steps.detail: The increased collision rate reduces the drift velocity ($v_d$); however, the thermal velocity ($v_t$) of the electrons increases with temperature.

questions.why: Higher temperature means more frequent electron–ion collisions (shorter relaxation time), lowering drift velocity, while random thermal speeds grow with temperature.

questions.prompt: For the given mixed combination of resistors, calculate the total resistance between points A and B.

steps.label: Top branch
steps.detail: Combine the two 4 $\Omega$ resistors in series at the top: $R_{s1} = 4 + 4 = 8\ \Omega$; this 8 $\Omega$ in parallel with the 8 $\Omega$ resistor gives $R_{p1} = 4\ \Omega$.

steps.label: Middle reduction
steps.detail: Combine that 4 $\Omega$ with the two side 4 $\Omega$ resistors in series: $R_{s2} = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12\ \Omega$; this 12 $\Omega$ in parallel with the 12 $\Omega$ resistor gives $R_{p2} = 6\ \Omega$.

steps.label: Final series sum
steps.detail: Combine the 6 $\Omega$ with the two 6 $\Omega$ legs in series: $R_{s3} = 6 + 6 + 6 = 18\ \Omega$.

questions.why: Repeated series–parallel reduction of the ladder (8∥8 → 4, then 4+4+4 = 12, 12∥12 → 6, then 6+6+6) gives 18 Ω between A and B.
questions.figure: Triangular resistor ladder between A (bottom left) and B (bottom right): top path has two 4 Ω in series; inner path has 4 Ω (left side), 8 Ω bridging horizontally in the middle, 4 Ω (right side); a 12 Ω bridges horizontally below; the two lower legs to A and B are 6 Ω each.

questions.prompt: A cell of emf 1.1 V and internal resistance 0.5 $\Omega$ is connected to a wire of resistance 0.5 $\Omega$. Another cell of the same emf is now connected in series with the intention of increasing the current but the current in the wire remains the same. The internal resistance of the second cell is ______.

steps.label: With second cell in series
steps.detail: Total emf $= E_1 + E_2 = 2.2$ V and total internal resistance $= r_1 + r_2$; current unchanged: $1.1 = 2.2/(0.5 + r_2 + 0.5)$.

steps.label: Solve
steps.detail: $1.1(1 + r_2) = 2.2 \Rightarrow r_2 = 1\ \Omega$.

questions.why: Doubling the emf while keeping the same 1.1 A current means the total resistance must also double from 1 Ω to 2 Ω, so the second cell's internal resistance is 1 Ω.

questions.prompt: P, Q, R, and S are four wires of resistances 3 $\Omega$, 3 $\Omega$, 3 $\Omega$, and 4 $\Omega$ respectively. They are connected to form the four arms of a Wheatstone bridge circuit. The resistance with which S must be shunted in order that the bridge may be balanced is ______.

steps.label: Balance condition
steps.detail: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge $P/Q = R/(S\|x)$, where $S\|x$ is S in parallel with the shunt x.

steps.label: Substitute
steps.detail: With P = Q = R = 3 $\Omega$ and S = 4 $\Omega$: $3/3 = 3/(4\|x)$, so $4\|x = 3\ \Omega$.

steps.label: Solve for x
steps.detail: $4x/(4 + x) = 3 \Rightarrow 4x = 12 + 3x \Rightarrow x = 12\ \Omega$.

questions.why: Balance requires the fourth arm to equal 3 Ω; shunting the 4 Ω wire with x must give 4x/(4+x) = 3, which solves to x = 12 Ω.

questions.prompt: Magnetic moment of a thin bar magnet is 'M'. If it is bent into a semicircular form, its new magnetic moment will be ______.

steps.label: Original moment
steps.detail: $M = m \times l$, the product of pole strength m and length l.

steps.label: Bend into semicircle
steps.detail: The length becomes the semicircular arc: $l = \pi r$, so $M = m\pi r$; the new pole separation is the diameter $2r$ (original length $l = \pi r$, so $2r = 2l/\pi$).

steps.label: New moment
steps.detail: $M' = m \times 2r = \dfrac{2}{\pi}M$.

questions.why: Bending shortens the effective pole-to-pole distance from the arc length πr to the diameter 2r, scaling the moment by 2/π: M′ = 2M/π.

questions.prompt: Ferromagnetic material used in Transformers must have ______.
options: Low permeability and High Hysteresis loss
High permeability and Low Hysteresis loss
High permeability and High Hysteresis loss
Low permeability and Low Hysteresis loss
questions.answer: (b) High permeability and Low Hysteresis loss

steps.label: Permeability requirement
steps.detail: High permeability allows the magnetic flux to pass through easily and ensures efficient operation.

steps.label: Hysteresis requirement
steps.detail: Low hysteresis loss minimizes energy losses during the magnetization and demagnetization cycles.

questions.why: A transformer core should channel flux easily (high permeability) and waste little energy per magnetization cycle (low hysteresis loss).

questions.prompt: A conducting ring of radius r is placed in a varying magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the ring. If the rate at which the magnetic field varies is x, the electric field intensity at any point of the ring is ______.

steps.label: Faraday's law
steps.detail: $\varepsilon = -d\Phi/dt$ with $\Phi = B\pi r^2$, so $\varepsilon = -\pi r^2 (dB/dt) = -\pi r^2 x$.

steps.label: Relate emf to E
steps.detail: $\varepsilon = E \times 2\pi r$.

steps.label: Solve
steps.detail: $E = \pi r^2 x/2\pi r = rx/2$.

questions.why: The induced emf πr²x is distributed around the circumference 2πr, so the induced electric field is E = rx/2.

questions.prompt: A 50 Hz AC current of crest value 1 A flows through the primary of a transformer. If the mutual inductance between the primary and secondary be 0.5 H, the crest voltage induced in the secondary is ______.
questions.answer: (c) 100 V (per the Answer Key; source anomaly — the paper's own explanation computes ≈157 V and concludes 'the closest option is 150 V', i.e. option (b))

steps.label: Induced voltage formula
steps.detail: $V_S = M(dI_p/dt)$; for $I_p = I_0\sin(\omega t)$ the maximum rate of change is $I_0\omega$.

steps.label: Substitute
steps.detail: $I_0 = 1$ A, $f = 50$ Hz, $\omega = 100\pi$ rad/s, so $dI_p/dt = 100\pi$ A/s.

steps.label: Compute
steps.detail: $V_s = 0.5 \times 100\pi = 50\pi \approx 157$ V; the explanation states the closest option is 150 V, yet the key marks (c) 100 V.

questions.why: The crest secondary voltage is M·ω·I₀ = 0.5 × 100π × 1 ≈ 157 V; the printed solution rounds to the closest option 150 V, but the printed answer key marks (c) 100 V — an internal inconsistency in the source.

questions.prompt: A long solenoid of diameter 0.1 m has $2 \times 10^4$ turns per meter. At the center of the solenoid, a coil of 100 turns and radius 0.01 m is placed with its axis coinciding with the solenoid axis. The current in the solenoid reduces at a constant rate to 0 A from 4 A in 0.05 s. If the resistance of the coil is $10\pi^2\ \Omega$, then the total charge flowing through the coil during this time is ______.

steps.label: Flux through the coil
steps.detail: $\Phi = B \times A = \mu_0 n I \pi r^2$ per turn; given $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ Tm/A, $n = 2 \times 10^4$ /m, $I = 4$ A, $r = 0.01$ m, $N = 100$.

steps.label: Rate of change
steps.detail: $dI/dt = (4 - 0)/0.05 = 80$ A/s, so $d\Phi/dt = \mu_0 n (dI/dt)\pi r^2 = 6.4\pi^2 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb/s.

steps.label: Induced emf
steps.detail: $\varepsilon = -N(d\Phi/dt) = -100 \times 6.4\pi^2 \times 10^{-3} = -0.64\pi^2$ V.

steps.label: Charge
steps.detail: $Q = \varepsilon\Delta t/R = 0.64\pi^2 \times 0.05/(10\pi^2)$; the explanation evaluates this to 32 $\mu$C (its intermediate exponent line is misprinted).

questions.why: The charge through the coil is Q = NΔΦ/R = N·μ₀n·ΔI·πr²/R = 100 × 4π×10⁻⁷ × 2×10⁴ × 4 × π×10⁻⁴ / (10π²) = 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ C = 32 μC.

questions.prompt: Lower half of a convex lens is made opaque. Which of the following statements describes the image of the object placed in front of the lens? A. No change in image. B. Image will show only half of the object. C. Intensity of image gets reduced.

steps.label: Full image still forms
steps.detail: When the lower half of a convex lens is made opaque, the lens still forms the complete image of the object.

steps.label: Intensity drops
steps.detail: Only half the lens converges light, so the amount of light passing through is reduced — the image intensity decreases, but the full object is still visible.

questions.why: Every part of a lens forms the whole image, so blocking half the lens only halves the light gathered: the complete image forms with reduced intensity.

questions.prompt: Two slits are made 0.1 mm apart and the screen is placed 2 m away. The fringe separation when a light of wavelength 500 nm is used is ______.

steps.label: Fringe-width formula
steps.detail: $\beta = \lambda D/d$ with $\lambda = 500 \times 10^{-9}$ m, $D = 2$ m, $d = 0.1 \times 10^{-3}$ m.

questions.why: Young's double-slit fringe width β = λD/d = (500 nm × 2 m)/(0.1 mm) = 10 mm = 1 cm.

questions.prompt: For an astronomical telescope having an objective lens of focal length 10 m and an eyepiece lens of focal length 10 cm, the telescope's tube length and magnification respectively are ______.
questions.why: In normal adjustment the tube length is fo + fe = 1010 cm and the magnification is fo/fe = 100.

questions.prompt: According to Bohr's Model: A. The radius of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to 'n'. B. The speed of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to '1/n'. C. The magnitude of the total energy of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to '$1/n^2$'. D. The radius of the orbiting electron is directly proportional to '$n^2$'.

steps.label: Radius
steps.detail: $r \propto n^2$, so statement (D) is correct and (A) — radius proportional to n — is incorrect.

steps.label: Speed and energy
steps.detail: $v \propto 1/n$ (statement B correct) and $|E| \propto 1/n^2$ (statement C correct).

steps.label: Conclude
steps.detail: Correct statements: (B), (C) and (D).

questions.why: Bohr's model gives r ∝ n², v ∝ 1/n and |E| ∝ 1/n², so B, C and D hold while A (r ∝ n) is false.

questions.prompt: For a full wave rectifier, if the input frequency is 50 Hz, the output frequency will be ______.

steps.label: Full-wave action
steps.detail: A full wave rectifier inverts every half cycle of the input AC signal, thereby doubling the frequency of the output signal.

steps.label: Compute
steps.detail: Output frequency $= 2 \times 50$ Hz $= 100$ Hz.

questions.why: A full-wave rectifier flips the negative half-cycles, producing two output humps per input cycle — the ripple frequency doubles to 100 Hz.

questions.prompt: For an electric dipole in a non-uniform electric field with dipole moment parallel to direction of the field, the force (F) and torque ($\tau$) on the dipole respectively are ______.

steps.label: Force in non-uniform field
steps.detail: The force on the dipole is non-zero ($F \neq 0$) because the field is non-uniform, causing a net force on the dipole.

steps.label: Torque when aligned
steps.detail: The torque is zero ($\tau = 0$) because the dipole is aligned with the field and there is no tendency to rotate.

questions.why: A field gradient pulls the two charges unequally (net force), but with p parallel to E the torque p × E vanishes.

questions.prompt: Two large plane parallel sheets shown in the figure have equal but opposite surface charge densities $+\sigma$ and $-\sigma$. A point charge q placed at points P1, P2, and P3 experiences forces F1, F2, and F3 respectively. Then:

steps.label: Outside the sheets
steps.detail: At $P_1$ (and likewise $P_3$) the fields of the two oppositely charged sheets cancel, so the point charge experiences no force: $F_1 = 0$, $F_3 = 0$.

steps.label: Between the sheets
steps.detail: At $P_2$ the fields due to both sheets are in the same direction and do not cancel, so $F_2 \neq 0$.

questions.why: For a pair of equal-and-opposite charged sheets the field is confined to the gap (σ/ε₀ between, zero outside), so only the charge at P2 feels a force.
questions.figure: Two vertical parallel sheets: left sheet +σ (plus signs), right sheet −σ (minus signs). Point charge q shown at P1 outside to the left of the positive sheet, P2 in the gap between the sheets, and P3 outside to the right of the negative sheet.

questions.prompt: Two charged metallic spheres with radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ are brought in contact and then separated. The ratio of final charges $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ on the two spheres respectively will be ______.

steps.label: Contact equalizes potential
steps.detail: In contact the spheres share charge until they reach the same potential; $V = Q/R$ for a sphere.

steps.label: Equate potentials
steps.detail: $V_1 = V_2 \Rightarrow Q_1/R_1 = Q_2/R_2$, hence $Q_1/Q_2 = R_1/R_2$.

questions.why: Touching conductors reach a common potential Q/R, so the final charges divide in proportion to the radii.

questions.prompt: Two charged particles, placed at a distance d apart in vacuum, exert a force F on each other. Now, each of the charges is doubled. To keep the force unchanged, the distance between the charges should be changed to ______.

steps.label: Coulomb's law
steps.detail: $F = k q_1 q_2/d^2$; doubling each charge gives $F' = k(4q_1q_2)/d'^2$.

steps.label: Keep force unchanged
steps.detail: $k(4q_1q_2)/d'^2 = k(q_1q_2)/d^2 \Rightarrow d'^2 = 4d^2 \Rightarrow d' = 2d$.

questions.why: Doubling both charges multiplies the numerator of Coulomb's law by 4, so the separation must double (d² → 4d²) to keep F the same.

questions.prompt: Two parallel plate capacitors of capacitances 2 $\mu$F and 3 $\mu$F are joined in series and the combination is connected to a battery of V volts. The values of potential across the two capacitors $V_1$ and $V_2$ and energy stored in the two capacitors $U_1$ and $U_2$ respectively are related as ______.

steps.label: Series → same charge
steps.detail: In series the charge Q on each capacitor is the same; $V_1 = Q/C_1 = Q/2$, $V_2 = Q/C_2 = Q/3$, so $V_1/V_2 = 3/2$.

questions.why: With equal series charge, both voltage and energy scale as 1/C, so V₁/V₂ = U₁/U₂ = C₂/C₁ = 3/2.

questions.prompt: Two resistances of 100 $\Omega$ and 200 $\Omega$ are connected in series across a 20 V battery as shown in the figure below. The reading in a 200 $\Omega$ voltmeter connected across the 200 $\Omega$ resistance is ______.

steps.label: Voltmeter loads the circuit
steps.detail: The 200 $\Omega$ voltmeter in parallel with the 200 $\Omega$ resistor gives an effective $R_2 = 100\ \Omega$.

steps.label: Voltmeter reading
steps.detail: $V = I \times 100\ \Omega = 10$ V (printed as $V_{200} = 1/10\ \text{A} \times 200\ \Omega$ across the combination position).

questions.why: The non-ideal voltmeter halves the 200 Ω branch to 100 Ω; the 20 V then divides equally between two 100 Ω sections, so the meter reads 10 V.
questions.figure: Series circuit: 20 V battery at the bottom drives 100 Ω and 200 Ω resistors in series; a voltmeter V of internal resistance 200 Ω (+ and − terminals marked) is connected across the 200 Ω resistor.

questions.prompt: The current through a 4/3 $\Omega$ external resistance connected to a parallel combination of two cells of 2 V and 1 V emf and internal resistances of 1 $\Omega$ and 2 $\Omega$ respectively is ______.
questions.why: The parallel cells reduce to Eeq = 5/3 V with req = 2/3 Ω; adding the 4/3 Ω load gives 2 Ω total, so I = (5/3)/2 = 5/6 A.

questions.prompt: A metallic wire of uniform area of cross-section has a resistance R, resistivity $\rho$, and power rating P at V volts. The wire is uniformly stretched to reduce the radius to half the original radius. The values of resistance, resistivity, and power rating at V volts are now denoted by R', $\rho$', and P' respectively. The corresponding values are correctly related as ______.

steps.label: Geometry after stretching
steps.detail: Radius halved → $A' = \pi(r/2)^2 = A/4$; constant volume → $L' = 4L$.

steps.label: New resistance
steps.detail: $R' = \rho L'/A' = \rho(4L)/(A/4) = 16\rho L/A = 16R$; resistivity is a material property, $\rho' = \rho$.

questions.why: Halving the radius quarters the area and (at constant volume) quadruples the length, so R grows 16×; resistivity is unchanged and at the same voltage P = V²/R falls to P/16.

questions.prompt: Three magnetic materials are listed below: A. Paramagnetics, B. Diamagnetics, C. Ferromagnetics. Choose the correct order of the materials in increasing order of magnetic susceptibility.

steps.label: Susceptibility by class
steps.detail: Diamagnetics: very small negative susceptibility (weakly repelled; e.g. bismuth, copper). Paramagnetics: small positive susceptibility (weakly attracted; e.g. aluminum, platinum). Ferromagnetics: very large positive susceptibility (strongly attracted; e.g. iron, nickel, cobalt).

steps.label: Order
steps.detail: Increasing susceptibility: Diamagnetics (B) < Paramagnetics (A) < Ferromagnetics (C).

questions.why: Susceptibility runs from slightly negative (diamagnets) through slightly positive (paramagnets) to very large positive (ferromagnets), giving order B, A, C.

questions.prompt: Two infinitely long straight parallel conductors carrying currents $I_1$ and $I_2$ are held at a distance d apart in vacuum. The force F on a length L of one of the conductors due to the other is ______.
options: proportional to L but independent of $I_1 \times I_2$
proportional to $I_1 \times I_2$ but independent of length L

steps.label: Ampère's force law
steps.detail: $F/L = (\mu_0/2\pi)(I_1 I_2)/d$ between two parallel conductors.

steps.label: Force on length L
steps.detail: $F = (\mu_0/2\pi)(I_1 I_2 L)/d$ — proportional to both the product of the currents and the length.

questions.why: The force per unit length between parallel currents is (μ₀/2π)I₁I₂/d, so the force on a stretch L scales with I₁·I₂·L.

questions.prompt: In the circuit shown below, a current 3I enters at A. The semicircular parts ABC and ADC have equal radii 'r' but resistances 2R and R respectively. The magnetic field at the center of the circular loop ABCD is ______.

steps.label: Current division
steps.detail: The 3I current divides inversely with resistance: I through ABC (2R) and 2I through ADC (R).

steps.label: Field of each semicircle
steps.detail: $B_{ABC} = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\mu_0 I}{2r} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$; $B_{ADC} = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\mu_0 2I}{2r} = \frac{2\mu_0 I}{4r}$.

steps.label: Net field
steps.detail: The fields oppose: $B_{total} = B_{ADC} - B_{ABC} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$; by the right-hand rule the net field is out of the plane.

questions.why: The branch currents (I and 2I) create opposing semicircular fields μ₀I/4r and 2μ₀I/4r at the center; the difference μ₀I/4r points out of the plane by the right-hand rule.
questions.figure: Circular loop with A (left), B (top), C (right), D (bottom). Current 3I enters at A from the left and exits at C to the right. Upper semicircle ABC has resistance 2R; lower semicircle ADC has resistance R; both have radius r.

questions.prompt: A square loop with each side 1 cm, carrying a current of 10 A, is placed in a magnetic field of 0.2 T. The direction of the magnetic field is parallel to the plane of the loop. The torque experienced by the loop is ______.

steps.label: Torque formula
steps.detail: $\tau = nIAB\sin\theta$ with n = 1, I = 10 A, $A = 1\ \text{cm}^2 = 1 \times 10^{-4}$ m², B = 0.2 T.

steps.label: Angle
steps.detail: Field parallel to the loop's plane → angle between the normal and the field is 90°, so $\sin\theta = 1$.

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.detail: $\tau = 1 \times 10 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.2 \times 1 = 2 \times 10^{-4}$ Nm.

questions.why: With B in the plane of the loop the torque is maximal: τ = IAB = 10 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.2 = 2 × 10⁻⁴ Nm.

questions.prompt: In an AC circuit, the current leads the voltage by $\pi/2$. The circuit is ______.
options: should have circuit elements with resistance equal to reactance

steps.label: Phase relations
steps.detail: Purely resistive: current and voltage in phase. Purely inductive: current lags voltage by $\pi/2$. Purely capacitive: current leads voltage by $\pi/2$.

steps.label: Match
steps.detail: Since the current leads the voltage by $\pi/2$, the circuit must be purely capacitive.

questions.why: A 90° current lead is the signature of a pure capacitor; inductors make current lag and resistors keep it in phase.

questions.prompt: In a pair of adjacent coils, for a change of current in one of the coils from 0 A to 10 A in 0.25 s, the magnetic flux in the adjacent coil changes by 15 Wb. The mutual inductance of the coils is ______.

steps.label: Definition
steps.detail: $M = \Delta\Phi/\Delta I$ — the ratio of flux change in one coil to the current change causing it.

questions.why: Mutual inductance is flux change per unit current change: 15 Wb / 10 A = 1.5 H (the 0.25 s is not needed).

questions.prompt: A wire of irregular shape in figure (a) and a circular loop of wire in figure (b) are placed in different uniform magnetic fields as shown in the figures below. In figure (a), the magnetic field is perpendicular into the plane. In figure (b), the magnetic field is perpendicular out of the plane. The wire in figure (a) is turning into a circular loop and that in figure (b) into a narrow straight wire. The direction of induced current will be ______.

steps.label: Figure (a)
steps.detail: Field into the plane; reshaping the irregular wire into a circle increases the enclosed area, increasing the inward flux. To oppose this increase, the induced current flows anticlockwise (producing a field out of the plane).

steps.label: Figure (b)
steps.detail: Field out of the plane; collapsing the circular loop into a straight wire decreases the enclosed area, decreasing the outward flux. To oppose this decrease, the induced current flows anticlockwise.

steps.label: Source note
steps.detail: The printed explanation's final sentence misstates 'clockwise in (a) and anticlockwise in (b)', contradicting its own body; the Answer Key marks (b): anticlockwise in both.

questions.why: By Lenz's law, (a) opposes growing inward flux with an outward-field (anticlockwise) current, and (b) opposes shrinking outward flux by sustaining it — also anticlockwise.
questions.figure: (a) An irregular dashed closed wire loop (points a, b, c, d) in a uniform field into the plane, being reshaped into a circular loop (area increases). (b) A circular loop (points a', b', c', d', with arrows showing it being flattened) in a uniform field out of the plane, being reshaped into a narrow straight wire (area decreases).

questions.prompt: Match List–I has four graphs showing variation of opposition to flow of AC versus frequency with circuit characteristic in List–II. List–II: (I) Impedance, (II) Capacitive reactance, (III) Inductive reactance, (IV) Resistance.

steps.label: Constant graph
steps.detail: Resistance (IV) remains constant with frequency → the horizontal line, graph (A).

steps.label: Rising line
steps.detail: Inductive reactance (III), $X_L = 2\pi fL$, increases linearly with frequency → straight line with positive slope, graph (B).

steps.label: Falling curve
steps.detail: Capacitive reactance (II), $X_C = 1/(2\pi fC)$, decreases hyperbolically with frequency → graph (C).

steps.label: Dip curve
steps.detail: Impedance (I) combines resistance and reactance without a simple linear/hyperbolic form (dips near resonance) → graph (D). (The printed final matching line misprints (B)–(II), (C)–(III); the key gives option (b).)

questions.why: Resistance is frequency-independent (flat), inductive reactance grows linearly, capacitive reactance falls as 1/f, and impedance shows the dipped curve — matching (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
questions.figure: List-I: four graphs of 'Opposition to act' vs frequency. (A) horizontal straight line (constant). (B) straight line rising from the origin. (C) hyperbolic curve decreasing with frequency. (D) curve that first falls then rises (a dip, as in series-resonance impedance).

questions.prompt: In an electromagnetic wave, the ratio of energy densities of electric and magnetic fields is ______.

steps.label: Stated result
steps.detail: The ratio of energy densities of the electric and magnetic fields in an electromagnetic wave is $1 : 1$.

steps.label: Reason
steps.detail: The wave carries its energy equally in the electric and magnetic fields ($\frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 = \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$ on average), so neither field dominates.

questions.why: In an EM wave the average electric and magnetic energy densities are exactly equal, so the ratio is 1 : 1.

questions.prompt: Of the following, the correct arrangement of electromagnetic spectrum in decreasing order of wavelength is ______.
options: Radio waves, X-rays, Infrared waves, microwaves, visible waves
Infrared waves, microwaves, Radio waves, X-rays, visible waves
Radio waves, microwaves, Infrared waves, visible waves, X-rays
X-rays, visible waves, Infrared waves, microwaves, Radio waves
questions.answer: (c) Radio waves, microwaves, Infrared waves, visible waves, X-rays

steps.label: Recall the spectrum
steps.detail: Across the electromagnetic spectrum, wavelength decreases from radio waves through microwaves, infrared and visible light to X-rays.

steps.label: Pick the matching option
steps.detail: From the given options, the correct arrangement in decreasing order of wavelength is: Radio waves, microwaves, Infrared waves, visible waves, X-rays.

questions.why: Wavelength shrinks along the spectrum from radio (longest) through microwaves, infrared and visible light down to X-rays (shortest of the listed).

questions.prompt: Match Electromagnetic waves listed in List–I with Production method/device in List–II. List–I: (A) Microwaves, (B) Infrared, (C) X-rays, (D) Radio waves. List–II: (I) LC oscillator, (II) Magnetron, (III) Vibration of atoms/molecules, (IV) Bombarding large atomic number metal target with moving electrons.

steps.label: Microwaves and infrared
steps.detail: Microwaves are commonly produced using a magnetron (electrons interacting with a magnetic field); infrared waves are produced by the vibration and rotation of atoms and molecules.

steps.label: X-rays and radio waves
steps.detail: X-rays are produced by bombarding a large atomic number metal target with fast-moving electrons; radio waves are commonly generated using an LC (inductor–capacitor) oscillator.

questions.why: Each wave has a standard production route: magnetron → microwaves, molecular vibration → infrared, electron bombardment of heavy metal targets → X-rays, LC oscillator → radio waves.

questions.prompt: In the figure given below, APB is a curved surface of radius of curvature 10 cm separating air and a transparent material ($\mu = 4/3$). A point object O is placed in air on the principal axis of the surface 20 cm from P. The distance of the image of O from P will be ______.
options: 16 cm left of P in air
16 cm right of P in water
20 cm right of P in water
20 cm left of P in air
questions.answer: (a) 16 cm left of P in air

steps.label: Solve
steps.detail: $v = -16$ cm; the negative value indicates the image is formed to the left of the surface — 16 cm left of P, in air.

questions.why: Refraction at the single spherical surface gives v = −16 cm; a negative image distance places the (virtual) image 16 cm to the left of P, on the air side.
questions.figure: Curved refracting surface APB (A top, P on the axis, B bottom), convex toward the left, separating air (left) from transparent material of μ = 4/3 (right). Point object O on the principal axis in air, 20 cm to the left of P.

questions.prompt: For fixed values of radii of curvature of lens, power of the lens will be ______.

steps.label: Lens maker's formula
steps.detail: $P = (\mu - 1)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2}\right)$, where $\mu$ is the refractive index and $R_1$, $R_2$ the radii of curvature.

steps.label: Fixed radii
steps.detail: With $R_1$ and $R_2$ fixed, $P \propto (\mu - 1)$.

questions.why: By the lens maker's formula, with the curvature factor fixed the power scales directly with (μ − 1).

questions.prompt: The graph correctly representing the variation of image distance 'v' for a convex lens of focal length 'f' versus object distance 'u' is ______.
options: Graph (a): hyperbolic branch in the fourth quadrant (positive u, negative v)
Graph (b): hyperbolic branch in the second quadrant (negative u, positive v)
Graph (c): straight line with positive slope through the origin
Graph (d): curve rising from the origin and saturating for positive u
questions.answer: (b) Graph (b): hyperbolic branch in the second quadrant (negative u, positive v)

steps.label: Lens formula
steps.detail: $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u}$, rearranged to $v = \dfrac{uf}{u - f}$.

steps.label: Shape and quadrant
steps.detail: The graph of this function is a hyperbola; it lies in the 2nd quadrant as u is negative (v positive).

questions.why: With the sign convention u < 0 for a real object and v > 0 for a real image, v = uf/(u−f) traces a hyperbola in the second quadrant — graph (b).
questions.figure: Four v-u graphs: (a) hyperbolic branch in the fourth quadrant (positive u, negative v) rising toward the u-axis; (b) axes with u increasing to the left — hyperbolic branch in the second quadrant (negative u, positive v) rising steeply near the v-axis; (c) straight line with positive slope through the origin; (d) curve from the origin rising and flattening (saturating) for positive u.

questions.prompt: Using light from a monochromatic source to study diffraction in a single slit of width 0.1 mm, the linear width of central maxima is measured to be 5 mm on a screen held 50 cm away. The wavelength of light used is ______.

steps.label: Central-maximum width
steps.detail: $\beta = \dfrac{2\lambda D}{a}$, so $\lambda = \dfrac{\beta a}{2D}$; given a = 0.1 mm, $\beta$ = 5 mm, D = 0.5 m.

questions.why: The single-slit central maximum has width 2λD/a; inverting with the measured 5 mm width gives λ = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m (500 nm).

questions.prompt: Radiation of frequency $2\nu_0$ is incident on a metal with threshold frequency $\nu_0$. The correct statement of the following is _____.
options: All photoelectrons emitted will have kinetic energy equal to $h\nu_0$
Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted can be $h\nu_0$
Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted will be $2h\nu_0$
questions.answer: (c) Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted can be $h\nu_0$

steps.label: Photon and threshold energies
steps.detail: Incident photon energy $E = h(2\nu_0)$; threshold energy $E_0 = h\nu_0$.

steps.label: Einstein's equation
steps.detail:
The excess energy becomes kinetic energy: $K.E._{max} = h(2
u_0) - h
u_0 = h
u_0$.

questions.why: By Einstein's photoelectric equation the maximum kinetic energy is hν − hν₀ = h(2ν₀) − hν₀ = hν₀; emitted electrons can have up to (not all exactly) this energy.

concept: NTA CUET (UG) Physics paper of 29 May 2024 — 50 MCQs (attempt 40, 5 marks each, −1 negative) covering modern physics, electrostatics, current electricity, magnetism, electromagnetic induction, AC, EM waves and optics. Answer key and worked explanations are transcribed from the paper itself.

mnemonics.expands: In any Bohr orbit, if the kinetic energy is K then potential energy is −2K and total energy is −K — the 1 : −2 : −1 ladder.
Magnetic susceptibility order: diamagnetic (small negative) < paramagnetic (small positive) ≪ ferromagnetic (large positive).
A full-wave rectifier flips every negative half cycle, so the output frequency is twice the input (50 Hz → 100 Hz).
Decreasing wavelength order of EM waves: radio > microwave > infrared > visible > X-rays.
